prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant produces compliant potable water; boundary River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood)–High Service Pump Header (Juniper); distribution excluded. Chief Operator authorizes manual/Storm Intake Mode/recovery, classifies upsets; automatic-control failure→Duty Engineer. Raw Water Screen Channel→Maintenance Planner (Quarry): Rake Torque Snapshot. Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold)→Alum Batch Ticket; Laboratory Technician verifies identity; Chief Operator approves dosing; inconsistent indications hold approved dose. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow) receives custody-controlled samples→checked Jar Test Photograph Set/analytical status; Laboratory Technician→Sample Chain Slip; release requires quality-control review. North Filter Gallery (Cobalt)/South Filter Gallery monitor turbidity/headloss; South→Filter Run Exception Note; Cobalt verifies capacity. Filter recovery requires wash/turbidity/valve/flow verification; breakthrough additionally approval/rinse-to-waste/stability. Backwash Recovery Tank receives washwater; return requires settling/sampling/clarity; Chief Operator→verified Backwash Solids Manifest. Chlorine Contact Basin/Clearwell Level Controller maintain contact/residual/storage/pumping alignment; controller→verified Clearwell Diver Entry Permit. Juniper→Pump Bearing Vibration Clip on exceedance. North Distribution Pressure Station monitors pressure/availability/communications; South Distribution Pressure Station starts booster after low-pressure delay. Distribution Dispatcher (Falcon) coordinates fieldwork/pumping→verified Pressure Zone Handoff Card. SCADA Historian Server links Sample Chain Slip/logs; retains operational records; critical asset. Control-room/crews coordinate radio/phone: station/valve identifiers, pressure-change direction, completion. Normal distribution restoration requires stable zones, cleared/assigned alarms, accounted fieldwork, no Chief Operator restrictions. Control system shall require named role-based operator/engineering/maintenance/read-only accounts; routine shared credentials prohibited; operators least-privilege; engineering changes separately approved. Remote access requires MFA/encryption/business-reason/Chief Operator-or-Duty Engineer approval. Quarry reviews maintenance access weekly/disables reassigned privileges. Segment control/administrative networks; document allowed historian/workstation/controller/support pathways; test patches/firmware/antivirus before deployment. Chief Operator owns alarm governance; Duty Engineer reviews limits/control changes/nuisance alarms. Priorities reflect consequence/response-time/action/capability-loss; Chlorine Residual Alarm remains high-priority for compliance/public-health concern. Shelving/suppression/disabling require

New part:
S213: During Storm Intake Mode, alarm response expectations shall account for higher debris load, faster raw water quality changes, and increased dependence on intake screening and chemical dose verification.
S214: Backup power shall support safe operation or controlled shutdown of the River Intake Pump Station, Raw Water Screen Channel, Chlorine Contact Basin, Clearwell Level Controller, SCADA Historian Server, High Service Pump Header, and essential control-room equipment.
S215: The plant shall maintain written expectations for generator start time, automatic transfer performance, fuel availability, and operator checks during extended utility outages.
S216: Uninterruptible power supplies shall be sized to bridge transfer events and allow orderly shutdown of servers, network switches, control processors, and communication equipment.
S217: Loss of both normal and standby power to a critical service shall be treated as an emergency operating condition requiring immediate notification of the Chief Operator and Duty Engineer.
S218: The Chief Operator has authority to direct emergency operating priorities when treatment, storage, distribution pressure, or personnel safety is at risk.
S219: The Duty Engineer may authorize temporary control workarounds during an emergency, but the workaround shall be logged, bounded by time or condition, and removed when normal control is restored.
S220: The Distribution Dispatcher shall be informed when failures at the High Service Pump Header, North Distribution Pressure Station, or South Distribution Pressure Station may affect pressure zones or fire-flow readiness.
S221: The Laboratory Technician shall retain access needed for sample status review and reporting, but laboratory accounts shall not allow control actions on plant equipment.
S222: The Maintenance Planner uses the permit to verify isolation boundaries before confined-space work is released.
S223: The Duty Engineer reviews the Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before accepting a change in chlorine storage status.
S224: Reliability targets for critical plant services shall include prompt detection of failed sensors, redundant communication paths where practical, recoverable configuration backups, and periodic restoration testing.
S225: After any cybersecurity event, major alarm failure, or emergency control action, the Chief Operator shall require a brief operational review that identifies the cause, affected services, corrective actions, and any needed procedure changes.
S226: Commissioning shall be planned as a controlled sequence that proves each control function before the plant relies on it for normal service.
S227: Each commissioning test shall have defined starting conditions, expected responses, acceptance limits, and a responsible reviewer.
S228: Before wet commissioning begins, the Duty Engineer shall confirm that temporary controls, bypasses, and manual operating instructions are understood by the affected staff.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
